resolution.note: planted-records stack timeout scales with host load per core, two stacks at a time; load-budget unit test

title: Ship scoped check fails planted-records init stacks on host load timeouts
body:
On 2026-11-17 `krn pr ship` for t-41d0vze refused the push: the scoped fast check failed 4 subtests of test/scripts/planted-records.test.ts ("every applicable enforced record bites in each init stack": ts, python, php, wp-plugin), each at the 240000 ms timeout, while host load average was ~100 (screening re-verify plus another lane fast check). The same file passed alone in 78 s (6/6). A ship refusal caused by host load costs a 25-minute rerun.
Outcome: the ship scoped check does not fail on load-bound timeouts: either planted-records runs its init stacks within budget under load (measured), or fast-check runs heavy files with bounded parallelism / reports a timeout as load, not as a red test.
Proof: node --test test/scripts/planted-records.test.ts passes under a synthetic load (e.g. stress with nproc workers) within its timeout, or fast-check reports a timeout separately; a test covers the chosen behavior.
